title: A Long-term Extension Study of Icotrokinra in Pediatric Participants
official: A Phase 3, Multicenter, Open Label, Basket, Long-term Extension Study of Icotrokinra in Pediatric Clinical Study Participants
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the long-term safety of icotrokinra in pediatric participants.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age <18 years old, at the time of first trial administration
2. Must have completed the dosage planned in the primary icotrokinra trial
3. Received benefit from continued icotrokinra therapy in the opinion of the investigator
4. Before enrollment, a female participant must be either: a. Not of childbearing potential OR b. Of childbearing potential and not sexually active, practicing abstinence or a highly effective method of contraception (failure rate of <1% per year when used consistently and correctly) and agrees to remain on a highly effective method while receiving trial intervention and until 90 days after the last dose - the end of relevant systemic exposure.
5. During the trial and for a minimum of 90 days after receiving the last dose of trial intervention, a male participant capable of producing sperm or ejaculate: a. who is sexually active with a female of childbearing potential must agree to use a barrier method of contraception (eg, condom with spermicidal foam/gel/film/cream/suppository) b. who is sexually active with a female who is pregnant must use a condom c. must agree not to donate sperm for 90 days after last dose of trial intervention
Exclusion criteria:
1. Is <18 years of age and in a location or territory where the trial intervention is approved for marketing authorization and reimbursed for the pediatric indication and their age.
2. Is pregnant, nursing, or planning pregnancy or planning to father a child
3. Employee of the investigator or trial site, with direct involvement in the proposed trial or other trials under the direction of that investigator or trial site, as well as family members of the employees or the investigator.
4. Any condition for which, in the opinion of the investigator, participation would not be in the best interest of the participant (eg, compromise the well-being) or that could prevent, limit, or confound the protocol-specified assessments.
